gap: At its peak (5.62-5.73) the leak is a milky near-white cream veil (brightest areas ~#fef1dd, saturation ~0.13 vs ~0.42 in the bar) that lifts the whole frame and blows the portrait out, so it reads as an overexposed white dissolve rather than amber sunlight (#ffc28a) flaring across a lens with a small hot core and saturated orange falloff.
notes: (1) Exposure decay is a step: strip mean luma 167 -> 190 -> 148 -> 79 -> 58 (5.51 to 5.94); it rises about +20 per frame but falls -42 then -69 between 5.73 and 5.84, so the room snaps in out of the haze instead of the flare easing off. (2) At 5.73 the room blacks are lifted to a flat muddy brown (~#6c533d over the left half) and the right-edge band is a desaturated grey-beige (~#ddccb6): foggy, not sunlit. (3) Good: the glow travels left to right (centre-left at 5.62, centre-right at 5.65, right edge at 5.73), the room window ghosting through the wall at 5.62 is a lovely bridge, and no frame goes flat (window, coursework card and GPA badge always read). (4) Room is established by 5.94: window, light shaft, SPEX card and copy; 6.05 matches. (5) Minor: a faint FINAL YEAR PROJECT kicker shows bottom-left over the about wall at 5.3 but not at 5.41 (maybe capture residue); body copy overlapping the window pane at 5.94/6.05 is room composition, not this element.
